description: The ‘backup’ probe is not a second sensor at all: every value is exactly the main probe’s reading converted to Fahrenheit (C × 9/5 + 32). Two probes in different spots would disagree by a few tenths of a degree; these never do. df.corr() puts them at 0.999 when every other pair tops out near 0.86, and (backup_probe_f − 32) × 5/9 − main_probe_c is zero on every row. The fake redundancy echoes a real lesson from Boeing’s 737 MAX, where MCAS acted on a single angle-of-attack sensor despite a second one being fitted; this pharmacy and its log are fictional.
hints: Two sensors that watch the same thing should agree roughly, but never perfectly. Look at how the numeric columns correlate with one another.
Compare the two cabinet probes directly: put them on the same scale and look at the difference, row by row.
Convert the backup probe to Celsius, (F − 32) × 5/9. It matches the main probe to the rounding on every single reading, so it is just a copy.
